**Architecture: Auto (Server + WebAssembly) render mode**
- First visit renders via Server-side for fast initial load
- Subsequent interactions run in WebAssembly — no server round-trips for UI, solving the worldwide latency issue
- Per-page `@rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly` on interactive pages

| Layer | What |
|-------|------|
| `ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/Dispatcher.razor` | Dispatcher dashboard — list, filter, create, update status |

| `ShipmentTracker/Endpoints/ShipmentEndpoints.cs` | Minimal API endpoints (role-protected) |
| `ShipmentTracker/Services/ServerShipmentService.cs` | EF Core-based data access |
| `ShipmentTracker/Data/SeedData.cs` | Roles (Dispatcher/Customer) + sample shipments |

**Auth:** ASP.NET Identity with individual accounts, role-based authorization (`Dispatcher` role for admin pages, any authenticated user for tracking).

Run with `dotnet run --project ShipmentTracker/ShipmentTracker` — the DB auto-migrates and seeds on startup.
